sourceEvidence.claim: The reversible cascade — ATP/ATPase pumps/cellular swelling as the earliest morphologic manifestation; ribosomal detachment; membrane blebbing; chromatin clumping; rapid functional loss (myocardial noncontractile after 1-2 minutes); myelin figures
sourceEvidence.quote:
▘ ↓ ATP → ↓ activity of Ca2+ and Na+/K+ -ATPase pumps → cellular swelling (cytosol,
mitochondria, endoplasmic reticulum/Golgi), which is the earliest morphologic manifestation
▘ Ribosomal/polysomal detachment → ↓ protein synthesis
▘ Plasma membrane changes (eg, blebbing)
▘ Nuclear changes (eg, chromatin clumping)
▘ Rapid loss of function (eg, myocardial cells are noncontractile after 1-2 minutes of ischemia)
▘ Myelin figures (aggregation of peroxidized lipids)
sourceEvidence.verifiedHow: pdftotext text-layer containment on pinned pages (verify-evidence.ts)

sourceEvidence.claim: The irreversible cascade — plasma membrane breakdown with troponin leak and Ca2+ influx; mitochondrial damage with ETC loss; lysosomal rupture with autolysis; the pyknosis-karyorrhexis-karyolysis ladder; amorphous densities
sourceEvidence.quote:
Irreversible cell injury

▘ Breakdown of plasma membrane → cytosolic enzymes (eg, troponin) leak outside of cell, influx
of Ca2+ → activation of degradative enzymes
▘ Mitochondrial damage/dysfunction → loss of electron transport chain → ↓ ATP
▘ Rupture of lysosomes → autolysis
▘ Nuclear degradation: pyknosis (nuclear condensation) → karyorrhexis (nuclear fragmentation
caused by endonuclease-mediated cleavage) → karyolysis (nuclear dissolution)
▘ Amorphous densities/inclusions in mitochondria

sourceEvidence.claim: Ferroptosis mechanism and morphology — lipid peroxidation, lethal lipid species, iron-dependent cell death; mitochondrial shrinkage with loss of cristae and outer membrane rupture
sourceEvidence.quote:
Lipid peroxidation → accumulation of lethal lipid species → iron-dependent cell death. Results in
shrinkage of mitochondria with loss of cristae and mitochondrial outer membrane rupture.
